$comment: wchar_t — the <stddef.h>/<stdlib.h> typedef AND the type of L'…'/L"…" — is the PLATFORM's type on every pair (P68 round 9, D-C-WCHAR-T-IS-SIGNED-ON-ARM64-LINUX): `int` on x86_64 Linux and macOS, `unsigned int` on aarch64 Linux, `unsigned short` on Windows. Both carriers now read ONE source, the target's `abiTypedefs.wchar_t` for the format (the table `__SIZEOF_WCHAR_T__` reads): the typedef names it (`abiTypedef`) and so do the wide literal-prefix rows. Six groups set six bits (main.c lists them); the exit is 42 only when all hold. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 at -O0 and -O2: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 on x86_64 Linux and on aarch64 Linux (cross, qemu) and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 all exit 42, and so does Apple clang 21.0.0 on arm64 and on x86_64 (the coordinator's Mac runs); MSVC 14.51 cannot compile it (no `__SIZEOF_WCHAR_T__`, the GNU predefine). ✔MEASURED at HEAD 4d9a24c4: on aarch64 Linux DSS's `wchar_t` and `L'a'` were `int` and `(wchar_t)-1 > 0` was FALSE (bits 4, 8 and 32 off → exit 19); the other pairs agreed. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE, ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 (each mutant compiled and run by DSS on pe64, ELF x86_64 and ELF aarch64 under qemu, debug and release): the wide literal rows without `abiTypedef` (their base core on every pair) exit 44 on pe (bits 1, 2 and 16 off) and 28 on aarch64 Linux (bits 1, 2 and 32 off), 42 on x86_64 Linux; <stddef.h>'s typedef back to per-format variants REFUSES the aarch64 build (F_ShippedTypeIdentityConflict — <stdlib.h> still reads the target) and leaves pe and x86_64 at 42. A per-format literal map cannot come back at all: the loader refuses `elementCoreByFormat`. The `release` arm runs the shipped optimizer pipeline over the same checks.
